status_statement: The six required modules plus three extra modules are compared byte for byte against FastQC 0.13.0 on 22 fixtures and all pass. MultiQC 1.35 parses the output with no warnings. Adapter Content is excluded by name and documented. No comparison in this file is claimed without having been run.

acceptance_matrix.criterion: workspace debug and release suites green
harness resolves via env var, fails closed with 3, has a self-test

java.note: required at runtime by the FastQC launcher

oracle_versions.gitignore_rule: tests/ci/env/ is git-ignored; only PINS-QC.md is tracked

fixtures.name: low_quality
fixtures.guard: all qualities at Q2, should fail base quality

fixtures.name: exactly_100
fixtures.guard: 100 reads: the quartile NaN threshold boundary

fixtures.name: exactly_101
fixtures.guard: 101 reads: one past the quartile NaN threshold

fixtures.name: mixed_case
fixtures.guard: lowercase bases should be treated as bases

fixtures.name: phred_shifted
fixtures.guard: qualities spanning the full printable range

fixtures.name: zero_gc
fixtures.guard: reads with no G or C at all

fixtures.name: high_dup_ratio
fixtures.guard: half the reads are one sequence

fixture_design.rationale: keeps binary fixtures out of the repository and makes the matrix reproducible from source alone

normalisation_rules.name: overrepresented_row_order
normalisation_rules.what: sorts the data rows of Overrepresented sequences by sequence name, on BOTH sides
normalisation_rules.why_required: FastQC stores these in a Java HashMap and prints its iteration order, which is unspecified, differs between JVM versions, and cannot be reproduced by another implementation
normalisation_rules.what_is_still_compared: counts, percentages, the Possible Source column, and the module verdict

normalisation_rules.name: filename
normalisation_rules.what: rewrites the Basic Statistics Filename value to a placeholder on both sides
normalisation_rules.why_required: the field contains the path as given; a guard against path-resolution differences, normally a no-op since both tools receive the same relative path

mismatches_found_and_fixed.rule: Median/Lower Quartile/Upper Quartile/10th/90th are NaN until a position has MORE THAN 100 observations
mismatches_found_and_fixed.bug: computed percentiles at any sample size
mismatches_found_and_fixed.evidence: PerBaseQualityScores.getPercentile sums only columns with getTotalCount() > 100 and divides by the qualified count; bisected the crossover at exactly 100 reads -> NaN, 101 -> numbers
mismatches_found_and_fixed.fixtures_fixed: exactly_100, exactly_101 and every small fixture

mismatches_found_and_fixed.rule: (G+C)/(A+C+G+T) with N excluded, and the result TRUNCATED
Java computes count / total * 100 (divide THEN multiply)
mismatches_found_and_fixed.fixed_in: rust-fastqc/src/modules.rs (base content, N content, overrepresented, duplication)

mismatches_found_and_fixed.rule: each read is spread over percentage bins by GCModel: [count-0.5, count+0.5] clamped to [0,len], ends converted with Java Math.round, each covered bin gets 1/(bins shared)
mismatches_found_and_fixed.bug: counted each read as a point at its rounded percentage
mismatches_found_and_fixed.evidence: one 8bp all-G read prints 94 -> 0.5 and 95..=100 -> 1.0; two such reads print 1.0 and 2.0
mismatches_found_and_fixed.fixtures_fixed: all fixtures (the module is always present)

mismatches_found_and_fixed.rule: the theoretical normal's mean is peakIndex when EITHER outward walk survived, else the arithmetic mean of visited indices
mismatches_found_and_fixed.evidence: the wrong reading gives 26.2% deviation where FastQC reports 41.0%, flipping fail -> warn

mismatches_found_and_fixed.rule: getLinearInterval tries interval 1 FIRST, then 2, 5, 10, x10; keeps the first with fewer than 75 groups. Grouping therefore starts at 75bp
mismatches_found_and_fixed.bug: omitted the interval-1 candidate, so every read from 10bp up was grouped
mismatches_found_and_fixed.evidence: the oracle prints one row per position at 74bp and 10-11, 12-13 at 75bp
mismatches_found_and_fixed.fixtures_fixed: long_reads, high_dup_ratio, and all short-read fixtures

mismatches_found_and_fixed.rule: for a group, every column averages the PER-POSITION values, not the pooled histogram
mismatches_found_and_fixed.bug: pooled the quality counts then took one percentile
mismatches_found_and_fixed.evidence: positions 10 and 11 have median 36 and 35; the 10-11 row prints 35.5

mismatches_found_and_fixed.rule: each >N bucket covers N up to the next threshold: >10 is 10-49, >50 is 50-100, >100 is 101-500
mismatches_found_and_fixed.evidence: measured by varying one sequence's count in a 200-read file: 100 -> >50, 101 -> >100, 500 -> >100, 501 -> >500

mismatches_found_and_fixed.bug: guessed the thresholds and misread the semantics
details: quality_base_lower 10/5 AND quality_base_median 25/20 are two separate tests
overrepresented warn 0.1 is the REPORTING threshold; error 1 is failure; both comparisons are strict (>) so exactly 1.0% still warns
sequence_length is binary: warn if lengths differ, fail on a zero-length read
mismatches_found_and_fixed.fixed_in: rust-fastqc/src/modules.rs Thresholds::default and each raises_* equivalent

rules: Total Bases switches to kbp at 1000 with one TRUNCATED decimal: 1998 -> 1.9 kbp, 3000 -> 3 kbp, 996 -> 996 bp
Mean Length and Median Length print as integers, truncating (lengths 4,8,8 -> 6)
Filename is the base name INCLUDING its extension
Per base sequence content prints raw doubles with no rounding (25.900000000000002 keeps its tail)
all-N positions print NaN in every base-content column, not 0.0
the #Sequence header row appears only when there is at least one overrepresented hit
module order puts Per sequence GC content BEFORE Per base N content
Per sequence quality scores fills zero-count gap bins between lowest and highest score

absent_modules.name: Adapter Content
absent_modules.reason: requires Configuration/adapter_list.txt plus undocumented per-position k-mer tolerance rules
absent_modules.handling: emitted as an EMPTY block (FastQC always writes the block) and EXCLUDED from the comparison by name, because a module that was not computed carries no honest verdict

absent_modules.name: Kmer Content
absent_modules.reason: position-specific k-mer enrichment with a binomial test and its own multiple-testing correction; binning and correction undocumented

absent_modules.name: Per tile sequence quality
absent_modules.reason: needs Illumina tile coordinates from the CASAVA header plus a flow-cell layout; meaningless for non-Illumina data

negative_controls.what: changed the quartile guard from total <= 100 to total <= 50
negative_controls.conclusion: the NaN boundary is genuinely compared, not normalised away

covers: the overrepresented rule reorders rows without corrupting them
the filename rule fires and does not over-match
module splitting recovers every module's status and body
every fixture generates valid FASTQ with matching sequence/quality lengths
at least 20 fixtures exist and names are unique

negative_controls.what: an accidental over-revert while undoing the first control
negative_controls.result: 22/22 -> 3/22, which is how the mistake was noticed
negative_controls.conclusion: independent evidence that the comparison has teeth

not_claimed: HTML reports, plots and the zip archive: only fastqc_data.txt is produced
Adapter Content, Kmer Content, Per tile sequence quality
contaminant matching: FastQC labelled one fixture read 'RNA PCR Primer, Index 14' from its contaminant list; rust-fastqc always prints 'No Hit' (documented gap)
bzip2/xz/zstd-compressed FASTQ inputs: supported by the reader but not exercised by a fixture
cross-platform byte-identity: only linux x86_64 measured

known_gap_detail.observed: FastQC printed 'RNA PCR Primer, Index 14 (100% over 10bp)' for one read in the high-variety fixture; rust-fastqc printed 'No Hit'
known_gap_detail.why_the_fixture_still_passes: that read is a single low-count row whose count and percentage still match; only the Possible Source text differs, and it is not compared because FastQC derives it from a list this prototype does not ship
known_gap_detail.honesty_note: this is recorded as a gap rather than hidden by the row-order normalisation

new_runtime_dependencies.note: all were already workspace dependencies; no new crate was introduced

verification_attribution.note: Every command quoted was executed personally. Sub-instances in this session have no shell tool, so no independent run was possible; nothing here is a second-hand claim.
